claims.claim: An alleged optimum has a linear-time verifiable certificate, even for arbitrary signed entries.
claims.evidence: For an alleged L, scanning every L-square proves feasibility, while one violating square for each length l>L proves that no larger length is feasible. A 2D prefix table makes each sum constant-time. There are at most mn L-square placements and at most q=min(m,n) witnesses, so verification takes O(mn) word operations without using sign monotonicity.
claims.witness: The certificate is the alleged L together with one coordinate pair for every l>L; no witness is needed for L because all its placements are scanned.
claims.search_method: Derived both certificate implications directly and exhaustively tested generated certificates, malformed alternatives, and signed matrices on 6,276 cases.

claims.claim: There is an exact output-sensitive search algorithm whose worst-case time is O(mn min(m,n)).
claims.evidence: Descending exhaustive search returns the first feasible length, hence the exact largest feasible length despite nonmonotonicity. For m>=n=q and d=q-L, its examined placements are bounded by sum_{t=0}^d (m-n+t+1)(t+1), which is O(mn+(m-n+1)(d+1)^2+(d+1)^3), at most O(mnq), and O(mn) for constant d. The L=0 expression merely adds a nonnegative fictitious side-zero term as an upper bound.
claims.witness: Direct enumeration agreed with the descending algorithm and its stated placement bound in all 6,276 tested searches.
claims.search_method: Checked correctness by descending-order quantifiers, expanded the placement-count sum, treated L=0 separately, and compared against brute force.

claims.claim: Feasibility can alternate at every side length, and the natural no-revisit greedy extension is incorrect.
claims.evidence: With first row 1,-1,1,-1,... and all other rows zero, every even-length row interval sums to zero, while odd-length intervals have maximum one; squares avoiding the first row contribute zero. Thus F_l is 0 for even l and 1 for odd l. In the 2x3 example, the side-2 sums are exactly 1 and 4, while the side-1 maximum is 2, so at k=1 no positive length is feasible; lowering at the second placement without revisiting the first misses the entry 2.
claims.witness: For A=[[2,1,1],[-3,1,1]] and k=1, F_1=2 and F_2=4, but the described no-revisit path accepts the first side-2 sum 1 and subsequently sees only entries at most 1.
claims.search_method: Computed the alternating family symbolically through interval parity and checked it through n=40; directly reproduced the greedy failure.

claims.claim: Any deterministic exact algorithm in the standard explicit one-word-per-entry cell-probe model requires Omega(mn) input probes in the worst case, even for Boolean matrices and k=0; thus an O(mn) algorithm would be optimal in this model.
claims.evidence: On the all-zero input the answer is q. Every cell (r,c) belongs to the in-bounds q-square starting at (min(r,m-q),min(c,n-q)). If that cell were unprobed, changing it alone to one would preserve the deterministic transcript but make that q-square violate k=0, changing the correct answer. Hence all mn cells must be probed on the zero input.
claims.witness: The stated placement formula was checked for every cell in every shape 1<=m,n<=30, totaling 216,225 coverage instances.
claims.search_method: Applied an adaptive-transcript indistinguishability adversary and separately audited rectangular, boundary, and q=1 cases.

claims.claim: The O(mn) endpoint is achievable for two nontrivial signed separable classes: multiplicative rank one and additive separability.
claims.evidence: For A_ij=u_i v_j, each square sum is a product of independent row- and column-window sums, whose maximum occurs among the four endpoint products. With pivot p, the corresponding square sum is XY/p; taking the maximum only after dividing all four candidates handles p<0 correctly. The pivot identities characterize rank at most one. For A_ij=u_i+v_j, F_l=l(max X_l+max Y_l). Prefix sums give O(m+n) work per length and q(m+n)<=2mn; recognition also costs O(mn).
claims.witness: Exact brute force matched the pivot-based formula on 2,560 signed rank-one instances and the additive formula on 648 signed separable instances, including negative pivots and zeros.
claims.search_method: Derived both factorization identities, audited recognition and negative-division order, and exhaustively compared their maxima with direct square enumeration.

claims.claim: If r rows and c columns are nonzero, there is an exact direct algorithm using O(mn+q min(rn,cm)) word operations; in particular, a constant number of nonzero rows or columns admits O(mn) time even with signed entries.
claims.evidence: For fixed l, supported row h contributes precisely for tops in [max(0,h-l+1),min(h,m-l)]. Its two endpoints generate O(r) grouped events. Updating all horizontal windows costs O(n) per event and scanning after each distinct event visits every realized active-row state, giving O(rn) per l. Empty states contribute exactly zero, whereas active all-negative states remain negative. Summing over q lengths and choosing the transposed orientation yields O(mn+q min(rn,cm)).
claims.witness: The event sweep matched brute-force maxima in 9,538 signed row- and column-oriented test instances, including simultaneous events, empty states, and all-negative active states.
claims.search_method: Proved the row-activity interval and state coverage, audited the valid-coordinate boundary and baseline cost, then performed exhaustive and seeded-random comparisons.

claims.claim: A thresholded max-plus-convolution scan embeds exactly into matrices supported on one row.
claims.evidence: For l=B-t, a first-row window beginning at s telescopes to p_{B-(t-s)}-p_s. When i=s and j=t-s are valid source indices, this equals C+x_i+y_j. If i>=N, it is at most C+W-H=-1; if j>=N, it is at most W-H<0. Both cannot be invalid because t<=2N-2. Valid values are at least C-2W=1, while squares avoiding the first row have value zero, so F_{B-t}=C+c_t exactly. The least t with c_t<=K therefore gives the largest feasible encoded length.
claims.witness: All 2,457 exact constructions tested—including N=1, extreme arbitrary middle-prefix values, signed vectors, and threshold values around every coefficient—matched the claimed identity and answer decoding.
claims.search_method: Expanded every telescoping endpoint, split all invalid-index cases, checked overwrites and boundary indices, then compared with direct square enumeration.

claims.claim: Any single-matrix reduction that represents N distinct source indices by N distinct positive side lengths must create a matrix with at least N^2 explicit cells.
claims.evidence: An m-by-n matrix has exactly q=min(m,n) positive square side lengths. Injectively assigning N source indices to distinct lengths forces q>=N. Since both dimensions are at least q, mn>=q^2>=N^2. The claim is correctly limited to explicit single-matrix, distinct-length decoding.
claims.witness: The inequality chain was checked across 1,600 dimension choices for N from 1 through 100.
claims.search_method: Audited the quantifiers and explicit-matrix restriction, then applied direct pigeonhole and dimension counting.

claims.claim: If integer bit lengths are unbounded and bit operations are charged, an O(mn) bound independent of bit length is impossible.
claims.evidence: For m=n=1, deciding the answer decides whether a<=k. On a=k=2^(B-1), every lower bit of a is zero. If a deterministic exact bit-probe execution omits lower position r, replacing a by k+2^r changes only that unobserved bit but reverses the comparison and the correct Max-Bounded-Sums answer. Thus the equality execution must inspect B-1 bits, giving Omega(B) bit cost although mn=1.
claims.witness: For bit lengths 2 through 256, all 32,640 alternatives differed from the equality input in exactly one lower bit and changed feasibility.
claims.search_method: Used a binary-input indistinguishability argument and checked every stated one-bit alternative over the tested bit-length range.

target_evidence: The draft supplies correct general verification and O(mnq) search, a matching input-reading lower bound, several O(mn) signed special cases, and structural reductions. It neither gives an O(mn) algorithm for unrestricted signed matrices in the unit-cost word/arithmetic model used by the source endpoint nor excludes one under a standard fine-grained hardness assumption. The unbounded-bit lower bound changes to explicit bit complexity and is only an input-length obstruction, as the draft itself states. Thus the exact source target remains unresolved, while the surviving results constitute material partial progress.
checks_performed: Read only /evidence/source.json and /evidence/parent.json; used no web or other evidence material.
